questions.q: The value of \(\tan\left(\cos^{-1}\dfrac45+\tan^{-1}\dfrac23\right)\) is
questions.sol: \(\cos^{-1}\frac45=\tan^{-1}\frac34\), so the value is \(\dfrac{\frac34+\frac23}{1-\frac12}=\dfrac{17}6\).

questions.q: The principal value of \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{2\pi}3\right)\) is
questions.sol: \(\sin\frac{2\pi}3=\sin\frac\pi3\) and \(\frac\pi3\in\left[-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right]\), so the value is \(\frac\pi3\).

questions.q: If we consider only the principle values of the inverse trigonometric functions then the value of \(\tan\left(\cos^{-1}\dfrac1{5\sqrt2}-\sin^{-1}\dfrac4{\sqrt{17}}\right)\) is
The no. of real solutions of \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x(x+1)}+\sin^{-1}\sqrt{x^2+x+1}=\dfrac\pi2\) is
questions.sol: We need \(x(x+1)\ge0\) and \(x^2+x+1\le1\), i.e. \(x(x+1)\le0\); so \(x(x+1)=0\). Both \(x=0\) and \(x=-1\) give \(0+\frac\pi2\).

questions.q: If \(\sin^{-1}\left(x-\dfrac{x^2}2+\dfrac{x^3}4-\ldots\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(x^2-\dfrac{x^4}2+\dfrac{x^6}4-\ldots\right)=\dfrac\pi2\) for \(0<|x|<\sqrt2\), then \(x\) equals
questions.sol: The two arguments must be equal: \(\dfrac x{1+\frac x2}=\dfrac{x^2}{1+\frac{x^2}2}\), i.e. \(2+x^2=x(2+x)\), so \(x=1\).

questions.q: The value of \(x\) for which \(\sin(\cot^{-1}(1+x))=\cos(\tan^{-1}x)\) is
If \(0<x<1\), then \(\sqrt{1+x^2}\left[\{x\cos(\cot^{-1}x)+\sin(\cot^{-1}x)\}^2-1\right]^{1/2}=\)
questions.sol: \(\cos(\cot^{-1}x)=\frac x{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\), \(\sin(\cot^{-1}x)=\frac1{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\): the brace is \(\sqrt{1+x^2}\), so the bracket is \(x^2\).

questions.q: The value of \(\cot\left\{\sum\limits_{n=1}^{23}\cot^{-1}\left(1+\sum\limits_{k=1}^n2k\right)\right\}\) is

For any \(y\in\mathbb R\), let \(\cot^{-1}(y)\in(0,\pi)\) and \(\tan^{-1}(y)\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then the sum of all the solutions of the equation \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6y}{9-y^2}\right)+\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9-y^2}{6y}\right)=\dfrac{2\pi}3\) for \(0<|y|<3\), is equal to
questions.sol: \(y>0\): both terms equal \(\tan^{-1}\frac{6y}{9-y^2}=\frac\pi3\), giving \(y^2+2\sqrt3y-9=0\), \(y=\sqrt3\). \(y<0\): \(\cot^{-1}(\cdot)=\pi+\tan^{-1}\frac{6y}{9-y^2}\), so \(\tan^{-1}\frac{6y}{9-y^2}=-\frac\pi6\), giving \(y^2-6\sqrt3y-9=0\), \(y=3\sqrt3-6\). Sum \(4\sqrt3-6\).

questions.q: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of \(\tan\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac35\right)-2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac2{\sqrt5}\right)\right)\) is
questions.sol: \(\tan A=\frac34\); \(\tan B=\frac12\), so \(\tan2B=\frac43\). \(\tan(A-2B)=\dfrac{\frac34-\frac43}{1+1}=-\dfrac7{24}\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha=3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac6{11}\right)\) and \(\beta=3\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac49\right)\), where the inverse trigonometric functions take only the principal values, then the correct option(s) is(are)
questions.sol: \(\frac12<\frac6{11}<\frac1{\sqrt2}\) gives \(\frac\pi2<\alpha<\frac{3\pi}4\): \(\cos\alpha<0\). \(0<\frac49<\frac12\) gives \(\pi<\beta<\frac{3\pi}2\): \(\cos\beta<0\), \(\sin\beta<0\). Then \(\frac{3\pi}2<\alpha+\beta<\frac{9\pi}4\): \(\cos(\alpha+\beta)>0\).

questions.q: For any positive integer \(n\), let \(S_n:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(S_n(x)=\sum\limits_{k=1}^n\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1+k(k+1)x^2}x\right)\), where for any \(x\in\mathbb R\), \(\cot^{-1}(x)\in(0,\pi)\) and \(\tan^{-1}(x)\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: The equation \(S_3(x)=\dfrac\pi4\) has a root in \((0,\infty)\)
questions.sol: Each term is \(\tan^{-1}(k+1)x-\tan^{-1}kx\), so \(S_n=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{nx}{1+(n+1)x^2}\). (a) true for \(n=10\). (b) \(\dfrac{1+(n+1)x^2}{nx}\to x\). (c) \(4x^2-3x+1=0\) has no real root. (d) the maximum of \(\tan S_n\) is \(\dfrac n{2\sqrt{n+1}}\), which is \(\frac34\) for \(n=3\).

questions.q: Solve the following equation for \(x\). \(\tan^{-1}2x+\tan^{-1}3x=\dfrac\pi4\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{5x}{1-6x^2}=1\) gives \(6x^2+5x-1=0\), \(x=\frac16\) or \(-1\); \(x=-1\) makes the left side negative.

questions.q: Find the value of \(\cos(2\cos^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}x)\) at \(x=\dfrac15\) where \(0\le\cos^{-1}x\le\pi\) and \(-\dfrac\pi2\le\sin^{-1}x\le\dfrac\pi2\)
questions.sol: \(2\cos^{-1}x+\sin^{-1}x=\frac\pi2+\cos^{-1}x\), so the value is \(-\sin(\cos^{-1}x)=-\sqrt{1-x^2}\).

questions.q: Prove that \(\cos(\tan^{-1}(\sin(\cot^{-1}x)))=\sqrt{\dfrac{x^2+1}{x^2+2}}\)
questions.sol: \(\sin(\cot^{-1}x)=\dfrac1{\sqrt{1+x^2}}=t\) and \(\cos(\tan^{-1}t)=\dfrac1{\sqrt{1+t^2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+x^2}{2+x^2}}\).

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) be three positive real numbers \(\theta=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{a(a+b+c)}{bc}}+\tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{b(a+b+c)}{ca}}+\tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{c(a+b+c)}{ab}}\) then \(\tan\theta\) equals .............
questions.sol: With \(s=a+b+c\) and \(x,y,z\) the three square roots: \(x+y+z=\dfrac{s^{3/2}}{\sqrt{abc}}=xyz\), so \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{x+y+z-xyz}{1-xy-yz-zx}=0\).

questions.q: The numerical value of \(\tan\left(2\tan^{-1}\dfrac15-\dfrac\pi4\right)\) is ..........
questions.sol: \(\tan\left(2\tan^{-1}\frac15\right)=\frac5{12}\); then \(\dfrac{\frac5{12}-1}{1+\frac5{12}}\).

questions.q: The greater of the two angles \(A=2\tan^{-1}(2\sqrt2-1)\) and \(B=3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac13\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac35\right)\) is ......
questions.sol: \(2\sqrt2-1>\sqrt3\), so \(A>\frac{2\pi}3\). \(3\sin^{-1}\frac13=\sin^{-1}\frac{23}{27}<\sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt3}2\) and \(\sin^{-1}\frac35<\frac\pi3\), so \(B<\frac{2\pi}3\).

questions.q:
Let \((x,y)\) be such that \(\sin^{-1}(ax)+\cos^{-1}(y)+\cos^{-1}(bxy)=\dfrac\pi2\).
Column IColumn II
(i) If \(a=1\) and \(b=0\), then \((x,y)\)(A) lies on the circle \(x^2+y^2=1\)
(ii) If \(a=1\) and \(b=1\), then \((x,y)\)(B) lies on \((x^2-1)(y^2-1)=0\)
(iii) If \(a=1\) and \(b=2\) then \((x,y)\)(C) lies on \(y=x\)
(iv) If \(a=2\) and \(b=2\), then \((x,y)\)(D) lies on \((4x^2-1)(y^2-1)=0\)
questions.sol: Write the equation as \(\cos^{-1}y+\cos^{-1}(bxy)=\cos^{-1}(ax)\) and take cosines: \(bxy^2-ax=\sqrt{(1-y^2)(1-b^2x^2y^2)}\); squaring gives the locus. (i) \(x^2=1-y^2\). (ii) \((1-y^2)(x^2-1)=0\). (iii) \(x^2+y^2=1\). (iv) \((1-y^2)(4x^2-1)=0\).

questions.q:
Match list-I with list-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists.
List-IList-II
(P) \(\left(\dfrac1{y^2}\left(\dfrac{\cos(\tan^{-1}y)+y\sin(\tan^{-1}y)}{\cot(\sin^{-1}y)+\tan(\sin^{-1}y)}\right)^2+y^4\right)^{1/2}\) takes value(1) \(\dfrac12\sqrt{\dfrac53}\)
(Q) If \(\cos x+\cos y+\cos z=0=\sin x+\sin y+\sin z\) then possible values of \(\cos\left(\dfrac{x-y}2\right)\) is(2) \(\sqrt2\)
(R) If \(\cos\left(\dfrac\pi4-x\right)\cos2x+\sin x\sin2x\sec x=\cos x\sin2x\sec x+\cos\left(\dfrac\pi4+x\right)\cos2x\) then possible value of \(\sec x\) is(3) \(\dfrac12\)
(S) If \(\cot\left(\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)=\sin\left(\tan^{-1}(x\sqrt6)\right)\), \(x\ne0\) then possible value of \(x\) is(4) \(1\)
questions.sol: (P) numerator \(\sqrt{1+y^2}\), denominator \(\dfrac1{y\sqrt{1-y^2}}\); the bracket is \((1-y^4)+y^4=1\). (Q) squaring and adding: \(\cos(x-y)=-\frac12\), so \(\cos\frac{x-y}2=\pm\frac12\). (R) reduces to \(\sin x(\cos x-\sin x)\left[\sqrt2(\cos x+\sin x)-2\right]=0\); \(\tan x=1\) gives \(\sec x=\sqrt2\). (S) \(\dfrac x{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\dfrac{x\sqrt6}{\sqrt{1+6x^2}}\) gives \(x^2=\frac5{12}\).

questions.q: Let \(f(\theta)=\sin\left(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sqrt{\cos2\theta}}\right)\right)\), where \(-\dfrac\pi4<\theta<\dfrac\pi4\). Then the value of \(\dfrac d{d(\tan\theta)}(f(\theta))\) is
questions.sol: If \(\tan\phi=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sqrt{\cos2\theta}}\) then \(\sin\phi=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sqrt{\sin^2\theta+\cos2\theta}}=\tan\theta\). So \(f(\theta)=\tan\theta\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[0,4\pi]\to[0,\pi]\) be defined by \(f(x)=\cos^{-1}(\cos x)\). The number of points \(x\in[0,4\pi]\) satisfying the equation \(f(x)=\dfrac{10-x}{10}\) is
questions.sol: \(f\) is \(x\), \(2\pi-x\), \(x-2\pi\), \(4\pi-x\) on the four intervals of length \(\pi\). Solving with \(1-\frac x{10}\): \(x=\frac{10}{11}\), \(x=\frac{10(2\pi-1)}9\), \(x=\frac{10(2\pi+1)}{11}\) lie in their intervals; \(x=\frac{10(4\pi-1)}9>4\pi\) does not.

questions.q:
The number of real solutions of the equation \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^\infty x^{i+1}-x\sum\limits_{i=1}^\infty\left(\dfrac x2\right)^i\right)=\dfrac\pi2-\cos^{-1}\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^\infty\left(-\dfrac x2\right)^i-\sum\limits_{i=1}^\infty(-x)^i\right)\) lying in the interval \(\left(-\dfrac12,\dfrac12\right)\) is _____ .
(Here, the inverse trigonometric functions \(\sin^{-1}x\) and \(\cos^{-1}x\) assume values in \(\left[\dfrac{-\pi}2,\dfrac\pi2\right]\) and \([0,\pi]\), respectively.)
questions.sol: Both sides are \(\sin^{-1}\) of the arguments: \(\dfrac{x^2}{1-x}-\dfrac{x^2}{2-x}=\dfrac x{1+x}-\dfrac x{2+x}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2}{(1-x)(2-x)}=\dfrac x{(1+x)(2+x)}\). So \(x=0\) or \(x^3+2x^2+5x-2=0\), an increasing cubic with one root in \(\left(0,\frac12\right)\). Two solutions.

questions.q: The value of \(\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac14\sum\limits_{k=0}^{10}\sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12}+\dfrac{k\pi}2\right)\sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12}+\dfrac{(k+1)\pi}2\right)\right)\) in the interval \(\left[-\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac{3\pi}4\right]\) equals _____.
questions.sol: \(\sec A\sec\left(A+\frac\pi2\right)=-\dfrac2{\sin2A}\) with \(2A=\frac{7\pi}6+k\pi\): each term is \(4(-1)^k\). The \(11\) terms add to \(4\), so the value is \(\sec^{-1}1=0\).

questions.q: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of \(\dfrac32\cos^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac2{2+\pi^2}}+\dfrac14\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2\sqrt2\pi}{2+\pi^2}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt2}\pi\) is ______.
questions.sol: Let \(\theta=\tan^{-1}\frac\pi{\sqrt2}>\frac\pi4\). The three terms are \(\frac32\theta\), \(\frac14(\pi-2\theta)\) (as \(\sin2\theta=\frac{2\sqrt2\pi}{2+\pi^2}\) with \(2\theta>\frac\pi2\)) and \(\frac\pi2-\theta\). Sum \(=\frac{3\pi}4\approx2.36\).

questions.q: Let \(\tan^{-1}(x)\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), for \(x\in\mathbb R\). Then the number of real solutions of the equation \(\sqrt{1+\cos(2x)}=\sqrt2\tan^{-1}(\tan x)\) in the set \(\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}2,-\dfrac\pi2\right)\cup\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\cup\left(\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{3\pi}2\right)\) is equal to
questions.sol: The equation is \(|\cos x|=\tan^{-1}(\tan x)\). On each interval put \(t=x+\pi,\ x,\ x-\pi\) respectively, so \(t\in\left(-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right)\) and the equation is \(\cos t=t\), which has exactly one solution. Total \(3\).

questions.q:
The total number of real solutions of the equation \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(2\tan\theta)-\dfrac12\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6\tan\theta}{9+\tan^2\theta}\right)\) is
(Here, the inverse trigonometric functions \(\sin^{-1}x\) and \(\tan^{-1}x\) assume values in \(\left[-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right]\) and \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), respectively.)
questions.sol: With \(t=\tan\theta\) and \(|t|\le3\): \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{6t}{9+t^2}=2\tan^{-1}\dfrac t3\), so \(\theta=\tan^{-1}2t-\tan^{-1}\dfrac t3\) and \(t=\dfrac{5t}{3+2t^2}\): \(t=0,\pm1\), giving \(\theta=0,\pm\dfrac\pi4\) (each checks). For \(|t|>3\) the equation becomes \(7t^2=2t^2-3\): no solution.

questions.q: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of \(\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11))+10\sin\left(2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)\right)+10\sin(2\tan^{-1}(2))\) is
